#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 Task 1.4 (FR-2, SDD D-2.1)
#
# execute-agent.sh applies a control arm's toggles to the sandbox copy only.
# Every assertion here reads the sandbox as the EXECUTOR saw it: the CLI stub
# snapshots CLAUDE.md, .claude/, .loa.config.yaml and the appended system
# prompt at the moment it starts (STUB_SNAPSHOT_DIR), after every
# materialisation step. The arm ids and toggles come from the real suite
# files; the prompt tree is a synthetic fixture so later prose edits to the
# live kernel cannot change what this test proves.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  EXEC="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh"
  REVIEW_SUITE="$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/review-recall.yaml"
  AUDIT_SUITE="$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/audit-recall.yaml"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/at.XXXXXX")"
  WS="$T/ws"; SNAP="$T/snap"
  mkdir -p "$WS"
  ( cd "$WS" && git init -q && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q --allow-empty -m init )
  export EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/claude-stub.sh"
  export EVAL_MODEL="claude-fable-5-1"
  export STUB_SNAPSHOT_DIR="$SNAP"
  unset LOA_EVAL_ARM LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT EVAL_EFFORT

  # --- synthetic prompt tree (the shape of 864069f2) ---
  PT="$T/tree"
  mkdir -p "$PT/.claude/loa" "$PT/.claude/rules" "$PT/.claude/data" \
    "$PT/.claude/skills/reviewing-code" "$PT/.claude/skills/auditing-security"
  printf '%s\n' "# Loa Framework Instructions" "" "## Three-Zone Model" "" "zones" "" \
    "## Karpathy Principles" "" "Every code-touching turn." "" "1. **Think before coding** — state assumptions." "" \
    "## Process Compliance" "" "rules" > "$PT/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
  echo "# Git Stash Safety" > "$PT/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md"
  echo "# Skill Frontmatter Invariants" > "$PT/.claude/rules/skill-invariants.md"
  printf '%s\n' "---" "paths:" '  - "grimoires/**"' "---" "# zone state" > "$PT/.claude/rules/zone-state.md"
  printf '%s\n' "---" "name: reviewing-code" "---" "# Review" "Review the diff." > "$PT/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md"
  printf '%s\n' "---" "name: auditing-security" "---" "# Audit" "" "### Coverage" "" \
    "Report every finding you actually observe." "" \
    "Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under" \
    "\`excluded\`, either confirm it or tally it as a finding of your own." "" \
    "## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally" "" "Count every finding." > "$PT/.claude/skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md"
  printf '%s\n' "flatline_protocol:" "  code_review:" "    enabled: true" "  security_audit:" "    enabled: true" > "$PT/.loa.config.yaml"
  ( cd "$PT" && git init -q && git add -A && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q -m tree )
  export EVAL_PROMPT_TREE="$PT"

  for s in reviewing-code auditing-security; do
    cat > "$T/task-$s.yaml" <<YAML
id: at-$s
schema_version: 1
skill: $s
category: skill-quality
fixture: hello-world-ts
description: "arm toggle task"
prompt: "Read the instructions and carry them out."
agent:
  skill: $s
  artifacts: [review.md]
graders:
  - type: code
    script: file-exists.sh
    args: ["review.md"]
YAML
  done
}

teardown() {
  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
}

run_arm() {  # run_arm <arm> <suite-file> <skill>
  LOA_EVAL_ARM="$1" LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE="$2" run "$EXEC" --task-yaml "$T/task-$3.yaml" --workspace "$WS"
}

@test "AT-1 both suites declare the canonical arm ids and the pre-registered threshold block" {
  [ "$(yq -r '[.ab.arms[].id] | join(",")' "$REVIEW_SUITE")" = "baseline,no_companion,no_karpathy,no_rule_files" ]
  [ "$(yq -r '[.ab.arms[].id] | join(",")' "$AUDIT_SUITE")" = "baseline,no_audit_delta" ]

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# evals/tests/run-arms.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 Task 1.6 (FR-2, SDD D-2.3)
#
# run-arms.sh drives control arms over a frozen fixture batch against a
# detached worktree pinned at --source-commit. The executor is the CLI stub
# (no model call); the source repo is a throwaway repo (LOA_ARMS_SOURCE_REPO)
# so no worktree is ever registered in the real repository; the results and
# the worktree live under the test's temp dir.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  RA="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/run-arms.sh"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ra.XXXXXX")"
  SRC="$T/src"
  mkdir -p "$SRC/.claude/loa" "$SRC/.claude/rules" "$SRC/.claude/skills/reviewing-code"
  printf '%s\n' "# Loa" "" "## Karpathy Principles" "" "k" "" "## Other" > "$SRC/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
  echo "# s" > "$SRC/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md"
  echo "# i" > "$SRC/.claude/rules/skill-invariants.md"
  printf '%s\n' "---" "name: reviewing-code" "---" "# Review" > "$SRC/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md"
  printf '%s\n' "flatline_protocol:" "  code_review:" "    enabled: true" > "$SRC/.loa.config.yaml"
  ( cd "$SRC" && git init -q && git add -A && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q -m src )
  SHA="$(git -C "$SRC" rev-parse HEAD)"
  export LOA_ARMS_SOURCE_REPO="$SRC" LOA_ARMS_CACHE="$T/cache"
  export EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/claude-stub.sh"
  # the stub writes a review that cites all three pr-01 defect anchors
  export STUB_WRITE_1='review.md::# Review\nhead/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:210 and head/.claude/scripts/lib/invoke-diagnostics.sh:50 and head/.claude/scripts/workflow-state.sh:72 and head/.claude/scripts/workflow-state.sh:400\n'
  RES="$T/results"
  unset STUB_FAIL_COUNTER LOA_EVAL_ARM LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES
}

teardown() {
  git -C "$SRC" worktree prune 2>/dev/null || true
  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
}

@test "RA-1 --dry-run lists the interleaved plan and writes MANIFEST.json without a worktree or a CLI call" {
  export STUB_ARGV_FILE="$T/argv"
  run "$RA" --suite review-recall --arms baseline,no_rule_files --fixtures pr-01,pr-02 --trials 2 \
    --source-commit "$SHA" --results-dir "$RES" --dry-run
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  grep -q 'planned trials: 8' <<<"$output"
  # trial-major, then fixture, then arm: arms alternate on consecutive lines
  [ "$(grep -E '^ +[0-9]+ ' <<<"$output" | awk '{print $2}' | head -4 | tr '\n' ,)" = "baseline,no_rule_files,baseline,no_rule_files," ]
  [ "$(grep -E '^ +[0-9]+ ' <<<"$output" | awk '{print $3}' | head -4 | tr '\n' ,)" = "pr-01,pr-01,pr-02,pr-02," ]
  M="$RES/review-recall/batch-pr-01-pr-02-n2/MANIFEST.json"
  [ -f "$M" ]
  [ "$(jq -r '.source_commit' "$M")" = "$SHA" ]
  [ "$(jq -r '.model_id' "$M")" = "global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5" ]   # the DEC-0172 default
  [ "$(jq -r '.dry_run' "$M")" = "true" ]
  [ "$(jq -r '.trials_planned' "$M")" = "8" ]
  [ "$(jq -r '.corpus.sha256 | length' "$M")" = "64" ]
  jq -e '.harness_commit and .executor.cli_version and .environment.os and .environment.yq' "$M" >/dev/null
  [ ! -e "$T/cache/arms-src-${SHA:0:12}" ]
  [ ! -e "$T/argv" ]
}

1	# Dockerfile.ablation — container executor image for the cycle-130 component ablation
     2	# (SDD D-4.9 / DEC-0411). Extends Dockerfile.sandbox's pinned base and non-root user
     3	# with the Claude Code CLI, the codex CLI, pytest and bats. It holds NO credentials.
     4	# pipeline-run.sh mounts exactly two host paths: the sandbox read-write at /workspace
     5	# and a per-run writable HOME at /home/evaluser (<run>/meta/home: the codex CLI's
     6	# auth.json/config.toml copies, empty .claude/ and .aws/; the CLI's session store). The
     7	# Bedrock route authenticates from AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK passed in the environment.
     8	# The image's tool versions (below) are the batch's versions: every arm runs here.
     9	#
    10	# Build (no build context is needed; nothing is COPY'd):
    11	#   docker build -t loa-ablation:258 - < evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation
    12	# Run:
    13	#   evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh --executor container --image loa-ablation:258 …
    14	#   (pipeline-run.sh passes --rm --name --user --network bridge --read-only --tmpfs /tmp
    15	#    --pids-limit 512 --memory 4g --cpus 2 and exactly the two mounts)
    16	#
    17	# Digest pinned 2026-02-11 (same base as Dockerfile.sandbox):
    18	#   docker manifest inspect node:20.11.0-bookworm-slim | jq '.manifests[0].digest'
    19	FROM rust:1-bookworm AS brbuild
    20	RUN cargo install beads_rust --version 0.2.6 --root /opt/br --locked 2>/dev/null || cargo install beads_rust --version 0.2.6 --root /opt/br
    21	
    22	FROM node:20.11.0-bookworm-slim@sha256:8ea90c4f037cc3c2f566eb46c53eaac005129113487eda4090058fe554578104 AS base
    23	
    24	ARG CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=2.1.299
    25	ARG CODEX_VERSION=0.162.1
    26	ARG PYTEST_VERSION=9.0.2
    27	ARG BATS_VERSION=v1.13.0
    28	
    29	RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    30	    bash \
    31	    git \
    32	    jq \
    33	    python3 \
    34	    python3-pip \
    35	    python3-venv \
    36	    grep \
    37	    diffutils \
    38	    coreutils \
    39	    procps \
    40	    ca-certificates \
    41	    curl \
    42	    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
    43	
    44	# yq (mikefarah/yq) with SHA256 integrity verification (as Dockerfile.sandbox)
    45	ARG YQ_VERSION=v4.40.5
    46	ARG YQ_SHA256_AMD64=0d6aaf1cf44a8d18fbc7ed0ef14f735a8df8d2e314c4cc0f0242d35c0a440c95
    47	ARG YQ_SHA256_ARM64=9431f0fa39a0af03a152d7fe19a86e42e9ff28d503ed4a70598f9261ec944a97
    48	RUN arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) && \
    49	    case "$arch" in \
    50	      amd64) yq_arch="amd64"; yq_sha256="${YQ_SHA256_AMD64}" ;; \
    51	      arm64) yq_arch="arm64"; yq_sha256="${YQ_SHA256_ARM64}" ;; \
    52	      *) echo "Unsupported architecture: $arch" && exit 1 ;; \
    53	    esac && \
    54	    curl -fsSL "https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/${YQ_VERSION}/yq_linux_${yq_arch}" \
    55	      -o /usr/local/bin/yq && \
    56	    echo "${yq_sha256}  /usr/local/bin/yq" | sha256sum -c - && \
    57	    chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq
    58	
    59	# The two CLIs at the versions the fingerprint pins (exact versions, no ranges).
    60	RUN npm install -g --no-fund --no-audit \
    61	      "@anthropic-ai/claude-code@${CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION}" \
    62	      "@openai/codex@${CODEX_VERSION}" \
    63	    && npm cache clean --force
    64	
    65	# pytest for Python fixtures (bookworm's pip is externally managed)
    66	RUN pip3 install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages "pytest==${PYTEST_VERSION}"
    67	# cheval's declared dependencies (.claude/adapters/pyproject.toml: dependencies + the `full` extra),
    68	# so the sandbox gates (adversarial-review.sh, flatline-orchestrator.sh) can dispatch (lead, DEC-0482)
    69	RUN pip3 install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages "rfc8785>=0.1.4" "jsonschema>=4.21" "pyyaml>=6.0" "httpx[http2]>=0.24.0"
    70	
    71	# bats-core at the pinned tag
    72	RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch "${BATS_VERSION}" https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core.git /tmp/bats-core && \
    73	    /tmp/bats-core/install.sh /usr/local && \
    74	    rm -rf /tmp/bats-core
    75	
    76	# Disable npm lifecycle scripts for anything the agent installs later
    77	RUN npm config set ignore-scripts true
    78	
    79	# Non-root user (as Dockerfile.sandbox). At run time /home/evaluser is replaced by the
    80	# per-run HOME bind mount and the process runs as the host uid (--user).
    81	RUN groupadd -r evaluser && useradd -r -g evaluser -d /home/evaluser -s /bin/bash evaluser
    82	# No beads (br) in the image: beads_rust 0.2.6 is not on crates.io and the host binary needs glibc 2.38+; the sandbox
    83	# materialiser writes the beads opt-out marker (LOA_EVAL_BR_BIN unset/absent), so every arm runs the skills'
    84	# markdown fallback alike (lead, Sprint 258).
    85	RUN mkdir -p /home/evaluser/.aws /home/evaluser/.claude /home/evaluser/.codex /workspace && \
    86	    chown -R evaluser:evaluser /home/evaluser /workspace
    87	
    88	ENV TZ=UTC
    89	ENV LC_ALL=C
    90	ENV HOME=/home/evaluser
    91	ENV NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=true
    92	ENV CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1
    93	
    94	USER evaluser
    95	WORKDIR /workspace
    96	
    97	# Health check — every tool the fingerprint names is present

# 1. Establish project root
    PROJECT_ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)

    # 2. Load integrity enforcement level
    ENFORCEMENT="warn"  # Default
    if [[ -f "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.loa.config.yaml" ]]; then
        ENFORCEMENT=$(grep "^integrity_enforcement:" "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.loa.config.yaml" | awk '{print $2}' || echo "warn")
    fi

    echo "Running pre-flight integrity checks (enforcement: ${ENFORCEMENT})..." >&2

    # 3. Verify System Zone checksums
    if [[ "${ENFORCEMENT}" != "disabled" ]] && [[ -f "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/checksums.json" ]]; then
        echo "Verifying System Zone integrity..." >&2

        # Simple check: compare file count (full SHA verification would be more thorough)
        EXPECTED_COUNT=$(jq -r '.files | length' "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/checksums.json" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
        # cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267): the manifest is generated from the TRACKED
        # .claude/ tree (tools/gen-checksums.sh), so count with the same rule:
        # git ls-files -- .claude minus overrides/ and the manifest. In a
        # submodule mount .claude/checksums.json links into the submodule; the
        # count is taken in the tree that owns the manifest.
        MANIFEST_TREE="${PROJECT_ROOT}"
        if [[ -L "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/checksums.json" ]]; then
            MANIFEST_LINK=$(readlink "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/checksums.json")
            [[ "${MANIFEST_LINK}" == /* ]] || MANIFEST_LINK="${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/${MANIFEST_LINK}"
            MANIFEST_TREE=$(cd "$(dirname "${MANIFEST_LINK}")/.." 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || MANIFEST_TREE="${PROJECT_ROOT}"
        fi
        ACTUAL_COUNT=0
        if git -C "${MANIFEST_TREE}" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            ACTUAL_COUNT=$(git -C "${MANIFEST_TREE}" ls-files -- .claude \
                | awk '!/^\.claude\/overrides\// && $0 != ".claude/checksums.json"' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
        fi
        # No tracked .claude/ in that tree (outside git, or a standard-mode
        # downstream that does not commit .claude/): keep the legacy count.
        if [[ "${ACTUAL_COUNT}" -eq 0 ]]; then
            ACTUAL_COUNT=$(find "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude" -type f ! -path "*/.git/*" ! -path "*/overrides/*" ! -path "*/checksums.json" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
        fi

        if [[ "${EXPECTED_COUNT}" != "${ACTUAL_COUNT}" ]]; then
            echo "⚠️  System Zone integrity check: file count mismatch" >&2
            echo "   Expected: ${EXPECTED_COUNT} files" >&2
            echo "   Actual:   ${ACTUAL_COUNT} files" >&2

            if [[ "${ENFORCEMENT}" == "strict" ]]; then
                echo "" >&2
                echo "SYSTEM ZONE INTEGRITY VIOLATION" >&2
                echo "" >&2
                echo "The .claude/ directory has been modified outside of the update process." >&2
                echo "" >&2
                echo "Resolution:" >&2
                echo "  1. Move customizations to .claude/overrides/" >&2
                echo "  2. Restore System Zone: .claude/scripts/update.sh --force-restore" >&2
                echo "  3. Re-run operation" >&2
                exit 1
            fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# freeze.sh — cycle-130 ablation suite freeze (SDD §5.13, DEC-0404, DEC-0414)
     4	#
     5	# Writes or verifies <root>/MANIFEST.sha256, the suite's frozen identity: one
     6	# "<sha256>  <relpath>" line per file under <root>/tasks/ (and <root>/smoke/
     7	# with --smoke), relpath relative to the root, LC_ALL=C sorted, sha256 (Python
     8	# hashlib: no harness script sources .claude/ code, eval.yml trust boundary).
     9	# validate-suite.sh runs first; an invalid suite is never frozen or accepted.
    10	#
    11	# Usage:
    12	#   freeze.sh [--root DIR] [--smoke] [--check] [--allow-partial] [--suite-file F]
    13	#
    14	#   --root DIR        suite root (default grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0)
    15	#   --smoke           cover smoke/ too (passed to the validator as well)
    16	#   --check           recompute and compare with MANIFEST.sha256; write nothing
    17	#   --allow-partial   passed to validate-suite.sh (fewer than four tasks per type)
    18	#   --suite-file F    passed to validate-suite.sh
    19	#
    20	# Output: `freeze: wrote MANIFEST.sha256 (N files, sha256 <digest of the manifest>)`
    21	# or `freeze: OK — N files match MANIFEST.sha256 (sha256 …)`; on drift every
    22	# changed / added / removed path on its own line.
    23	#
    24	# Exit: 0 written / matches; 1 drift, missing manifest under --check, or the
    25	#       validator found violations; 2 usage.
    26	# Tested by evals/tests/freeze.bats.
    27	# =============================================================================
    28	set -euo pipefail
    29	export LC_ALL=C
    30	
    31	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    32	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    33	
    34	ROOT="$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0"
    35	CHECK=false SMOKE=false
    36	VARGS=()
    37	
    38	usage() { sed -n '2,/^# =====.*$/p' "$0" | sed -n '2,26p' | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2; }
    39	die() { echo "freeze: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    40	
    41	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    42	  case "$1" in
    43	    --root) ROOT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    44	    --smoke) SMOKE=true; VARGS+=(--smoke); shift ;;
    45	    --check) CHECK=true; shift ;;
    46	    --allow-partial) VARGS+=(--allow-partial); shift ;;
    47	    --suite-file) [[ -n "${2:-}" ]] || die "--suite-file needs a path"; VARGS+=(--suite-file "$2"); shift 2 ;;
    48	    --help|-h) usage ;;
    49	    *) die "unknown option: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    50	  esac
    51	done
    52	[[ -n "$ROOT" && -d "$ROOT" ]] || die "suite root not found: ${ROOT:-<empty>}"
    53	ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd)"
    54	MANIFEST="$ROOT/MANIFEST.sha256"
    55	
    56	vrc=0
    57	"$SCRIPT_DIR/validate-suite.sh" --root "$ROOT" ${VARGS[@]+"${VARGS[@]}"} || vrc=$?
    58	if [[ $vrc -eq 1 ]]; then echo "freeze: refused — the suite does not validate" >&2; exit 1; fi
    59	[[ $vrc -eq 0 ]] || die "validate-suite.sh failed (exit $vrc)"
    60	
    61	# compute_manifest <out> — the manifest body for the current tree.
    62	compute_manifest() {
    63	  local out="$1" list dirs=(tasks)
    64	  [[ "$SMOKE" == "true" ]] && dirs+=(smoke)
    65	  list="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/freeze-list.XXXXXX")"
    66	  local d
    67	  for d in "${dirs[@]}"; do
    68	    [[ -d "$ROOT/$d" ]] || continue
    69	    ( cd "$ROOT" && find "$d" -type f -print )
    70	  done | LC_ALL=C sort > "$list"
    71	  if grep -q '\\' "$list"; then rm -f "$list"; die "a path under the suite holds a backslash"; fi
    72	  python3 -I - "$ROOT" "$list" > "$out" <<'PY' || { rm -f "$list"; die "hashing failed"; }
    73	import hashlib, os, sys
    74	root, listing = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    75	for rel in open(listing, encoding="utf-8").read().splitlines():
    76	    if not rel:
    77	        continue
    78	    h = hashlib.sha256()
    79	    with open(os.path.join(root, rel), "rb") as f:
    80	        for b in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
    81	            h.update(b)
    82	    print(h.hexdigest() + "  " + rel)
    83	PY
    84	  rm -f "$list"
    85	}
    86	digest_of() { python3 -I -c 'import hashlib, sys; print(hashlib.sha256(open(sys.argv[1], "rb").read()).hexdigest())' "$1"; }
    87	
    88	TMP="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/freeze.XXXXXX")"
    89	trap 'rm -f "$TMP"' EXIT
    90	compute_manifest "$TMP"
    91	n="$(grep -c . "$TMP" || true)"
    92	
    93	if [[ "$CHECK" == "true" ]]; then
    94	  [[ -f "$MANIFEST" ]] || { echo "freeze: no MANIFEST.sha256 in $ROOT (run freeze.sh first)" >&2; exit 1; }
    95	  if cmp -s "$TMP" "$MANIFEST"; then
    96	    echo "freeze: OK — $n files match MANIFEST.sha256 (sha256 $(digest_of "$MANIFEST"))"
    97	    exit 0
    98	  fi
    99	  echo "freeze: DRIFT against $MANIFEST:"
   100	  python3 -I - "$MANIFEST" "$TMP" <<'PY'
   101	import sys
   102	def load(p):
   103	    m = {}
   104	    for line in open(p, encoding="utf-8"):
   105	        line = line.rstrip("\n")
   106	        if line:
   107	            h, _, rel = line.partition("  ")
   108	            m[rel] = h
   109	    return m
   110	old, new = load(sys.argv[1]), load(sys.argv[2])
   111	for rel in sorted(set(old) | set(new)):
   112	    if rel not in new:
   113	        print(f"  removed  {rel}")
   114	    elif rel not in old:
   115	        print(f"  added    {rel}")
   116	    elif old[rel] != new[rel]:
   117	        print(f"  changed  {rel}")
   118	PY
   119	  exit 1
   120	fi
   121	
   122	cp "$TMP" "$MANIFEST.tmp" && mv "$MANIFEST.tmp" "$MANIFEST"
   123	echo "freeze: wrote MANIFEST.sha256 ($n files, sha256 $(digest_of "$MANIFEST"))"
   124	exit 0
   125	#!/usr/bin/env bash
   126	# =============================================================================
   127	# fingerprint.sh — toolchain fingerprint for ablation runs (cycle-130 FR-4, SDD A11 / DEC-0389)
   128	#
   129	# Prints `fp:<sha256>` over the LC_ALL=C-sorted `tool=version` lines of the
   130	# toolchain an ablation run depends on (claude, codex, python3, node, yq, jq,
   131	# bats, git, docker) plus `source_tree=<HEAD of --source-tree>`. A tool that is
   132	# not installed reads `tool=absent`, so a missing tool changes the fingerprint
   133	# instead of failing the run. The value fills `image_digest` in host mode and
   134	# `fingerprint` in every mode (MANIFEST.json, pipeline.json, runs.jsonl). It reads the
   135	# HOST toolchain: in container mode the phases run on the image's toolchain, and the
   136	# image digest (not this value) identifies the batch's versions (on 2026-10-15 the host
   137	# CLI was 2.1.300 while Dockerfile.ablation pins 2.1.299).
   138	#
   139	# Usage:
   140	#   fingerprint.sh [--source-tree DIR] [--claude-bin B] [--bats-bin B] [--json]
   141	#
   142	# Options:
   143	#   --source-tree DIR  the pinned Loa tree; its `git rev-parse HEAD` is folded in
   144	#                      (`none` when absent or not a git tree)
   145	#   --claude-bin B     the CLI executable (default: $EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN, else claude)
   146	#   --bats-bin B       bats executable (default: bats on PATH, else the operator's
   147	#                      ~/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats)
   148	#   --json             print {fingerprint, tools{}, source_tree, lines[]} instead
   149	#
   150	# Exit codes:
   151	#   0  printed
   152	#   2  usage error
   153	#
   154	# Tested by evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats (fingerprint cases).
   155	# =============================================================================
   156	set -euo pipefail
   157	export LC_ALL=C
   158	
   159	# Hashing is Python hashlib: no harness script sources .claude/ code (eval.yml
   160	# "Validate grader trust boundary").
   161	
   162	SOURCE_TREE=""
   163	CLAUDE_BIN="${EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN:-claude}"
   164	BATS_BIN="${LOA_EVAL_BATS_BIN:-}"
   165	JSON=false
   166	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
   167	  case "$1" in
   168	    --source-tree) SOURCE_TREE="${2:?--source-tree needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
   169	    --claude-bin)  CLAUDE_BIN="${2:?--claude-bin needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
   170	    --bats-bin)    BATS_BIN="${2:?--bats-bin needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
   171	    --json)        JSON=true; shift ;;
   172	    -h|--help)     sed -n '2,28p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
   173	    *) echo "fingerprint.sh: unknown argument: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
   174	  esac
   175	done
   176	if [[ -z "$BATS_BIN" ]]; then
   177	  if command -v bats >/dev/null 2>&1; then BATS_BIN=bats
   178	  else BATS_BIN="$HOME/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats"; fi
   179	fi
   180	
   181	# first line of `<bin> <args>`, whitespace collapsed; `absent` when not runnable
   182	tool_version() {  # tool_version <bin> <args...>
   183	  local bin="$1"; shift
   184	  if ! command -v "$bin" >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ ! -x "$bin" ]]; then printf 'absent'; return 0; fi
   185	  local out
   186	  out="$("$bin" "$@" 2>&1 < /dev/null || true)"
   187	  out="$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n '1p' | tr -s ' \t' ' ' | sed 's/^ //; s/ $//')"
   188	  [[ -n "$out" ]] || out="unknown"
   189	  printf '%s' "$out"
   190	}
   191	
   192	lines="$(
   193	  {
   194	    printf 'claude=%s\n'  "$(tool_version "$CLAUDE_BIN" --version)"
   195	    printf 'codex=%s\n'   "$(tool_version codex --version)"
   196	    printf 'python3=%s\n' "$(tool_version python3 --version)"
   197	    printf 'node=%s\n'    "$(tool_version node --version)"
   198	    printf 'yq=%s\n'      "$(tool_version yq --version)"
   199	    printf 'jq=%s\n'      "$(tool_version jq --version)"
   200	    printf 'bats=%s\n'    "$(tool_version "$BATS_BIN" --version)"
   201	    printf 'git=%s\n'     "$(tool_version git --version)"
   202	    printf 'docker=%s\n'  "$(tool_version docker --version)"
   203	  } | LC_ALL=C sort
   204	)"
   205	src="none"
   206	if [[ -n "$SOURCE_TREE" ]]; then
   207	  src="$(git -C "$SOURCE_TREE" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo none)"
   208	fi
   209	lines="$lines"$'\n'"source_tree=$src"
   210	digest="$(printf '%s\n' "$lines" | python3 -I -c 'import hashlib, sys; print(hashlib.sha256(sys.stdin.buffer.read()).hexdigest())')"
   211	fp="fp:$digest"
   212	
   213	if [[ "$JSON" == true ]]; then
   214	  printf '%s\n' "$lines" | jq -Rn --arg fp "$fp" --arg src "$src" '
   215	    [inputs | select(length > 0)] as $l
   216	    | {fingerprint: $fp, source_tree: $src, lines: $l,
   217	       tools: ($l | map(select(startswith("source_tree=") | not) | capture("^(?<k>[^=]+)=(?<v>.*)$") | {(.k): .v}) | add)}'
   218	else
   219	  printf '%s\n' "$fp"
   220	fi

Write your findings to \`review.md\` at the repository root: one line per finding as \`head/<path>:<line> — <description>\` with line numbers from the \`pr/head/\` files, and a final line \`Verdict: APPROVED\` or \`Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED\`."
    else
      tc="$(jq -r '.test_command // [] | if type == "array" then join(" ") else . end' <<<"$TASK_JSON")"
      contract="Test command: \`$tc\`. Write your changes in place; run the tests; stop when they pass."
    fi
    tpl="$(subst "$tpl" TASK_TEXT "$text")"
    tpl="$(subst "$tpl" CONTRACT "$contract")"
  fi
  tpl="$(subst "$tpl" SPRINT "$SPRINT")"
  tpl="$(subst "$tpl" TASK_ID "$TASK_ID")"
  tpl="$(subst "$tpl" FLATLINE "$FLATLINE")"
  tpl="$(subst "$tpl" CHANGE_NOTE "$CHANGE_NOTE")"
  printf '%s\n' "$tpl" > "$out"
}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# =============================================================================
3	# validate-suite.sh — cycle-130 ablation task-suite validator (SDD §3.2, DEC-0424)
4	#
5	# Checks every task of the ablation-2.0 suite before it is frozen, run or graded.
6	#
7	# Usage:
8	#   validate-suite.sh [--root DIR] [--smoke] [--allow-partial] [--suite-file F]
9	#
10	#   --root DIR        suite root (default grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0); the
11	#                     tasks are <root>/tasks/<id>/task.yaml
12	#   --smoke           also validate <root>/smoke/<id>/task.yaml (never counted)
13	#   --allow-partial   skip the four-by-four type count (Sprint 258 state)
14	#   --suite-file F    suite yaml (default evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml): arm ids
15	#                     for the leakage check, arms' task_types, suite_version
16	#
17	# Checks (each violation is one stdout line `<task-id>: <reason>`):
18	#   1. schema: id (= directory name), schema_version 1, type (feature-build |
19	#      bug-fix | refactor | review-catch), source {kind, date, fix_commit?,
20	#      base_commit?, bead?, origin?}, post_cutoff (bool), fixture (dir under the
21	#      root; null only for review-catch), criterion (agent-facing; no path, file
22	#      name or test name), success_criterion, test_command (array; null only for
23	#      review-catch), regression_command (array | null), reference_patch (hidden/…
24	#      | null; required for bug-fix and feature-build), grader_protected (array of
25	#      relative paths present in the fixture), structural_check (hidden/… | null;
26	#      required for refactor), bounds {max_turns{}, timeout_min{}} (phase → positive
27	#      int), review_catch (null, or {fixture, manifest, labels?} for review-catch,
28	#      both present), suite_version (= the suite file's), TASK.md present
29	#   2. counts: four tasks of each type under tasks/ (unless --allow-partial)
30	#   3. allowlist: test_command[0] and regression_command[0] in python3 | pytest |
31	#      bats | bash | node | npx
32	#   4. hidden/manifest.json (build types): {"files": [{src, dest}]}; every src
33	#      exists under hidden/; every dest is relative, inside the tree, no `..`
34	#   5. fixture path rule (build types): check_fixture_path_rule from
35	#      lib/sandbox-mount.sh — no .claude/, CLAUDE.md, .loa.config.yaml, grimoires/
36	#      or .run/ at the fixture's top level; the reference patch touches none either
37	#   6. leakage: TASK.md and criterion (the task-brief text is built from these)
38	#      and every phase prompt under evals/harness/lib/phase-prompts/ contain none
39	#      of: the string `hidden` (any case), a hidden test file's stem, a defect id
40	#      of the review manifest, a `D[0-9]{2}-` key, an arm id of the suite file
41	#   7. suite file: every non-absent arm's task_types are known (all | build |
42	#      review-catch | feature-build | bug-fix | refactor)
43	#
44	# Exit: 0 valid; 1 violations (every one listed); 2 usage / unreadable input.
45	# Tested by evals/tests/validate-suite.bats.
46	# =============================================================================

# options (the caller runs under `set -euo pipefail`).
#
# Contract (every function returns 0 on success, 2 when refused / when a step
# cannot take effect; refusals name the reason on one stderr line):
#
#   mount_prompt_surface <ws> <prompt_tree> <skill|->
#       skill given: <ws>/.claude/skills/<skill>/ (whole dir), .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md,

#       .loa.config.yaml only in arm mode (LOA_EVAL_ARM set), as cycle-129 did.
#       skill "-": the whole .claude/ tree is copied (files, never a symlink to the
#       tree), CLAUDE.md as above, and .loa.config.yaml always (the pipeline
#       executor needs every skill, hook and script). Evidence: mount=skill:<s>|tree.
#   resolve_arm_toggles <arm> <suite_file>
#       prints the arm's toggles as compact JSON on stdout. Arms are read from
#       `.arms[]` (ablation-2.0) and `.ab.arms[]` (recall suites). An arm with
#       toggles {} (a1_full, baseline) prints {}; `baseline` undeclared prints {}.
#       Exit 2: undeclared arm (an unreadable suite file declares none), `absent: true` arm.
#   apply_arm_toggles <ws> <toggles_json> <arm>
#       applies every toggle to the SANDBOX COPY and verifies it afterwards; exit 2
#       when one cannot take effect or is unknown. Toggles and values:
#         companion_voice: false  flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice=false
#         karpathy_block: false   '## Karpathy Principles' out of CLAUDE.loa.md (+ constraints.json rows)

#                                 LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false exported in the CALLING shell

content.text:
I found six defects in my scope. One will very likely make the new CI gate fail on this PR itself. Two things checked out:

- **Hashes and generated files match.** The sha256 of `head/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml` is `ba767f53…122c`, which matches the `.checksum` file. Both `sha256` entries in `.build-manifest.json` match the real hashes of `config.generated.ts` and `truncation.generated.ts`. `source_hash` equals `sha256` of the `"<sha256>  <path>"` lines, in both base and head. The new gpt-6.1-sol values are the same everywhere: the YAML, `generated-model-maps.sh`, the TS/JS registries and the truncation tables.
- **Versions agree.** `.loa-version.json`, the `CLAUDE.loa.md` header and the ablation suite comment all say `2.0.0-rc.5`.

In `/tmp/scratch-b`, using a stub `sha256_portable` (`sha256sum "$@"`), the three new bats files pass. The exceptions are MP-6, which needs the real repo, and GC-7/MP-7, which fail only because my `TMPDIR` is inside a git repo.

### Findings (paths relative to /workspace/pr/head/)

**1. High (likely; I can't prove it from the snapshot): `.claude/checksums.json` isn't regenerated, so the new gate fails on this PR**
- Where: `.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:177-178`; `tests/unit/check-manifest-paths.bats:88-92` (MP-6)
- The PR changes at least 16 tracked `.claude/` files: model-config.yaml and its .checksum, CLAUDE.loa.md, check-loa.sh, preflight.sh, generated-model-maps.sh, 9 bridgebuilder files and the pricing test. It never touches `.claude/checksums.json`.
- If the manifest is committed (MP-6 and `--help` say it is), `gen-checksums.sh --check` will report `changed:` for each of those files and exit 1.
- If it isn't committed, `check-manifest-paths.sh` exits 2 with "manifest not found", and MP-6 fails.
- If it was last written by the old `find`-walk generators (the #1267 problem this PR fixes), MP-6 also fails on untracked entries.
- The header of `tests/unit/gen-checksums.bats:8-9` says "the live manifest is only read by GC-8", but there is no GC-8. That looks like a live-manifest test was removed.
- Caveat: the snapshot holds only the 72 changed files. If the manifest was regenerated but left out of review scope, this finding goes away.

**2. Medium: `check-manifest-paths.sh` wrongly flags non-ASCII and `"` paths as untracked**
- Where: `tools/check-manifest-paths.sh:80`
- `git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -- .claude` runs without `-z`, so git's default `core.quotePath` C-quotes paths with non-ASCII bytes or `"`. `gen-checksums.sh` reads with `-z` and writes the raw keys; it only rejects newline, tab and backslash.
- Reproduced: a repo with `.claude/café.md` and `.claude/a"b.md`. `gen-checksums.sh` and `--check` both succeed. `check-manifest-paths.sh` then exits 1 with `2 untracked (other=2)`, and its "regenerate with gen-checksums.sh" advice can't fix it.
- Fix: use `ls-files -z | tr '\0' '\n'` (paths with newlines are already refused), or `-c core.quotePath=false`.

**3. Medium: the workflow's path filters don't cover the new gate or the new eval step**
- Where: `.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:23-46` (push) and `:49-72` (pull_request)
- Neither list includes `.claude/checksums.json`, `tools/gen-checksums.sh`, `tools/check-manifest-paths.sh`, `evals/**`, `.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/**` or `.claude/loa/**`.
- So a PR that only edits the manifest, the gate scripts, a bridgebuilder or `loa/` file (which changes the manifest), or only `evals/**` never triggers this workflow. Manifest drift gets merged unchecked, and the new "Run eval harness tests" step never runs for evals-only changes.

**4. Low-Medium: preflight's file count can disagree with the generator, and strict mode exits 1**
- Where: `.claude/scripts/preflight.sh:189-191` vs `tools/gen-checksums.sh:96-100`
- Preflight counts every `git ls-files -- .claude` entry. The generator skips tracked paths that aren't regular files: symlinks to directories, gitlinks, dangling symlinks, and files deleted from the working tree.
- Reproduced: a tracked `.claude/link -> d` symlink gives manifest length 1 but preflight's count 2. That's a "file count mismatch", and `exit 1` under `integrity_enforcement: strict`.
- Preflight needs the same `-f` filter.

**5. Low: `fresh-mount-proof.sh --worktree` keeps files deleted with `git rm`**
- Where: `tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh:133`
- `git ls-files --cached --others` doesn't list paths removed from the index (`git rm`, or the old name after `git mv`). The overlay never deletes them, so they stay in the temp upstream commit taken from REF.
- Verified: after `git rm .claude/b`, only `.claude/a` is listed.
- So the proof runs against a tree that still has files the change deletes.

**6. Low: setup-step failures in `fresh-mount-proof.sh` can go unnoticed**
- Where: `tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh:105` with `overlay` (`:122-136`) and `init_downstream` (`:144-149`)
- `run_step` calls these functions inside `if ! "$@"`, which turns off `set -e` inside them. Only the last command's status counts.
- In `overlay`, a failed `cp`, `mkdir` or `git add -A` is ignored, and `git commit --allow-empty` still succeeds. The proof then reports success on a mount without the work-tree state, with no exit 3.

**Also (Low, test fragility):** GC-7 (`tests/unit/gen-checksums.bats:86-91`) and MP-7 (`tests/unit/check-manifest-paths.bats:99-102`) assume the bats temp dir isn't inside a git work tree. With `TMPDIR` inside a repo (as in this environment, `/workspace/.eval/tmp`), the "not a git work tree" checks fail. They pass with `TMPDIR=/tmp`.

I found six real defects in my scope. The most serious is that the extraction is not behaviour-neutral: a failed copy into the sandbox no longer stops `execute-agent.sh`. Paths are relative to `/workspace/pr/head/`.

**Extraction check.** Moving the code into `evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh` mostly kept behaviour. I ran base and head side by side with a stub CLI for the companion_voice, karpathy_block, rule_files, audit_delta_instruction and `{}` arms. The toggled files, `.loa.config.yaml` and `skill-prompt.md` came out the same; only the evidence and checksums file differ (finding 2). Note that `/workspace/pr/head` holds only the changed files, so `bats evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats` can't run there: AT-16 through AT-24 fail on missing `.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh` and similar. I tested the functions in isolation instead.

### Findings

**1. HIGH — a failed copy into the sandbox is ignored and the agent runs anyway.**
- `evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:207` (call site); the unchecked copies are in `evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:144-155`.
- In base these copies ran at the top level under `set -euo pipefail`, so any failure stopped the script.
- In head the copies live inside `mount_prompt_surface`, which is called as `... || exit 2`. Bash turns off `set -e` inside a function called that way.
- The copies at lines 144, 146, 150, 152 and 154 have no `|| return 2`, so the function always returns 0.
- Reproduced: I made one file in the prompt tree's `.claude/rules/` unreadable. Base printed the `cp` error and exited 1 without starting the CLI. Head printed the same error, exited 0 and ran the CLI with that rule file missing from the sandbox.
- The arm then silently runs on an incomplete prompt surface. This breaks the lib's own contract (header lines 11-12: "2 when a step cannot take effect").

**2. LOW — the "WITHOUT behaviour change" claim is false for cycle-129 arm runs.**
- `evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:214-222`; the claim is at `evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:6-7`.
- In arm mode every run now gets a new `.claude/checksums.json`, and `arm_evidence` gains `manifest_files` and `manifest_sha256`. This includes the cycle-129 baseline arm, whose `arm_evidence` used to be `{}`.
- Arm mode also now unsets an inherited `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE`.
- Confirmed by the side-by-side runs: the toggles behave the same, but the sandbox contents and evidence differ. The execute-agent header documents these additions; the lib header's claim does not hold.

**3. MEDIUM — toggles write through symlinks to files outside the sandbox.**
- `evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:131` (`cp -a` keeps symlinks), `:235` (`cat "$tmp" > "$f"`), `:342` (`printf > "$mc.checksum"`), `:391` (`find -type f` skips symlinks).
- Reproduced: I made a prompt-tree `SKILL.md` an absolute symlink to a file outside the tree, then ran the whole-tree mount (skill `-`) with `{"effort":"medium"}`. The `effort:` line was removed from the outside file itself.
- The regenerated manifest showed `files: {}`, so the integrity check never covers symlinked files.
- This contradicts header line 18 ("files, never a symlink to the tree") and "toggles hit the SANDBOX COPY only". The eval workflow mounts a PR-controlled `.claude/`, which makes this a real trust-boundary issue.

**4. MEDIUM — several new assertions in `evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats` can never fail.**
- Bats does not fail a test on a `! cmd` line, or on a failure early in an `a && b` line, unless it is the last line of the test. I confirmed this on bats 1.13.0 with a three-case test file.
- Lines that can't fail:
  - **294, 295:** a0 has no `--append-system-prompt-file` and no `--effort`.
  - **313:** no `effort:` left in the sandbox `SKILL.md`.
  - **361:** "an inherited override never reaches an arm that did not declare it".
  - **481:** no arm id or "hidden" in the grimoire.
  - **292, 293, 327, 485, 486:** `[ ] && [ ]` chains; only the last check counts, and only when the earlier ones pass. This includes the A2 and build "no sprint.md" checks.
- The base file already uses this pattern (lines 132, 133, 152, 153, 166). The new tests extend it to the gate-leak and leak-guard claims. Fix with `run !`, `|| false`, or one check per line.

**5. LOW — `evals/tests/fixtures/mount-lib-stub.sh` differs from the real library, so `pipeline-run.bats` can't catch contract drift.**
- Stub line 24 emits `mount=whole_tree`; the real lib (line 134) emits `mount=tree`. `evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats:245` asserts `whole_tree`, a value production never produces.
- Stub `write_sandbox_grimoire` (lines 106-108) writes `sprint.md` for review-catch even when the arm sets `sprint_plan: false`; the real lib (lines 451-477) does not.
- Stub `apply_arm_toggles` silently ignores unknown toggles, never checks that a toggle took effect, and names its evidence `effort_stripped` where the lib uses `effort_skills_stripped`.

**6. LOW/MEDIUM — `evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation` has an unpinned, dead build stage and unpinned Python packages.**
- **Lines 19-20:** the `FROM rust:1-bookworm AS brbuild` stage uses a floating tag with no digest. It installs `beads_rust 0.2.6`, which line 82 says "is not on crates.io". Nothing copies from this stage (there is no `COPY --from`). BuildKit skips it, but the legacy builder (`DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0`) runs it and fails.
- **Line 69:** `rfc8785>=0.1.4`, `jsonschema>=4.21`, `pyyaml>=6.0` and `httpx[http2]>=0.24.0` are ranges, not pins. That contradicts line 8 ("the image's tool versions (below) are the batch's versions"), and a rebuild picks up different versions.
- The base image digest, non-root `USER evaluser` and yq checksum check look correct.

### Checked and found clean
- **Phase prompts (`evals/harness/lib/phase-prompts/*.md`):** every placeholder is filled by `build_prompt` in `pipeline-run.sh` (lines 534-554). I first suspected that `&` in task text would be mangled during substitution; `pipeline-run.sh:120` disables the bash option that causes it (`shopt -u patsub_replacement`), so it is not a defect. The fallback to `task-brief.md` when there is no sprint plan is consistent across PLAN, IMPLEMENT, REVIEW, FIX and AUDIT. I found no contradictions.
- **`evals/tests/fixtures/docker-stub.sh` and `claude-stub-pipeline.sh`:** no defects found.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# tools/gen-checksums.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.1, DEC-0368)
#
# Writes the System Zone integrity manifest `.claude/checksums.json` from the
# TRACKED `.claude/` tree only. The legacy generators (mount-loa.sh and
# update.sh `generate_checksums`) walk the working tree with `find`, so build,
# cache and runtime artefacts (`__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `node_modules`,
# `.run/`) that exist only on the generating machine end up in the manifest and
# read as Missing on every fresh mount. This generator lists
#
#   git -C ROOT ls-files -z -- .claude
#
# minus every path under `.claude/overrides/` (user-owned) and minus the
# manifest itself (`.claude/checksums.json`), hashes each with
# `sha256_portable` (.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh) and writes
#
#   {"generated": "<UTC ISO-8601>", "algorithm": "sha256",
#    "files": {"<path>": "<sha256 hex>", ...}}
#
# pretty-printed by jq (2-space), keys in `LC_ALL=C` byte order. Two runs on
# the same tree are byte-identical except `generated`. The working-tree content
# of each tracked path is hashed (an unstaged edit is reflected); a tracked
# path deleted from the working tree is skipped with a warning on stderr.
#
# Usage:
#   tools/gen-checksums.sh [--root DIR] [--out FILE]   # (re)generate
#   tools/gen-checksums.sh --check [--root DIR] [--out FILE]
#
# Options:
#   --root DIR   repository work tree to read (default: the git top level of
#                the current directory)
#   --out FILE   manifest path (default: ROOT/.claude/checksums.json). With
#                --check this is the committed manifest that is compared.
#   --check      regenerate to a temp file and compare its `files` map with
#                the manifest at --out; nothing is written
#   -h, --help   this text
#
# Exit codes:
#   0  generated, or --check: the `files` maps are identical
#   1  --check: drift (the first ten differing paths, each labelled added /
#      removed / changed, on stderr) or the manifest is absent / not JSON
#   2  usage error, ROOT is not a git work tree, or a tracked path name that
#      cannot be represented safely (newline, tab or backslash)
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C

SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=../.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh
source "${SELF_DIR}/../.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"

usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
die2() { echo "gen-checksums: $*" >&2; exit 2; }

MANIFEST_REL=".claude/checksums.json"
ROOT=""
OUT=""
CHECK=0
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do

content.text:
I found 8 defects in the scoped files. The most serious is that `integrity_clean` can be passed with a tampered `.claude/` tree. Everything was checked in a scratch copy; nothing under `/workspace/pr` was touched.

**What I could and couldn't run:**
- **Passed:** `took-effect.bats` (21), `ablation-row.bats` (18) and `spend.bats` (6), all on jq 1.7.1. The fixture run directories (`evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/runs/`) aren't in the PR tree, so I rebuilt them with `regen.sh` first. jq 1.6 is the system default here, so I used a downloaded jq 1.7.1 (deleted afterwards).
- **Not run:** `validate-suite.bats`, `freeze.bats` and `run-arms.bats`. The trees given to me are missing the smoke tasks under `grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke`, `.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh` and the review-recall fixtures. Findings for those files come from reading the code.

## Findings

**1. `evals/harness/took-effect.sh:239-240, 265-266` — `integrity_clean` never checks the trusted digest (high)**
- The rule requires `arm_evidence.manifest_sha256` to be present. That value is the harness's sha256 of `checksums.json` at mount time (`regen_sandbox_manifest` in `lib/sandbox-mount.sh`).
- But the rule only compares it to the current file's hash to decide whether to add "(matches checksums.json)" to the evidence (line 266). A mismatch still returns OK.
- So an agent that edits a `.claude/` file and also rewrites the matching entry in the agent-writable `sandbox/.claude/checksums.json` passes.
- Reproduced: after appending to `.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md` and updating its hash in `checksums.json`, the output was `integrity_clean OK 5 manifest entries verified; manifest_sha256 8c267cb13e8a` and `arm a1_full: OK`, exit 0.
- Files added under `.claude/` that aren't in the manifest are also never detected, because the walk only covers manifest entries.
- Fix: fail when `filesha != msha`.

**2. `evals/harness/run-arms.sh:454` (effect at 506-508) — a failed first attempt's cost is dropped from the spend cap (med)**
- On a transport retry, `run_trial` resets `executor='null'`, so the row carries only attempt 2's `executor.json`.
- `collect` adds only `.executor.total_cost_usd` to `SPENT`, so whatever attempt 1 spent is lost.
- If attempt 2 fails at sandbox creation, the row's cost is 0 even though attempt 1 spent money.
- Result: `--max-usd` under-counts and can overshoot the cap. This contradicts the header's "spent = executor-reported total_cost_usd of … completed and failed rows".

**3. `evals/tests/freeze.bats:38` and `:79` — two assertions can never fail (med)**
- `! grep -qv …` and `! grep -q '  smoke/' …` are not the last command in their tests. Bash's errexit ignores `!` pipelines, and bats doesn't catch them either.
- Confirmed with bats 1.13: a test containing `! true` followed by `true` reports `ok`.
- So the manifest line-format check and the "smoke files are outside the manifest" check are not tested. Use `run ! grep …` or `[ -z "$(grep …)" ]`.

**4. `evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:285` — fails to compile on jq 1.6 (low-med)**
- In jq 1.6, `label` is a keyword, so the object shorthand `{name, label, session_id, …}` is a syntax error.
- Verified with jq 1.6: `syntax error, unexpected ',', expecting ':' … line 58`. The script exits 3, which isn't one of its documented exit codes (0/1/2), and every row build fails.
- Writing `label: .label` works on both versions. jq 1.6 is still the default on Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04.
- Outside my scope: `pipeline-run.sh` also breaks on jq 1.6 (`$label`), which made `regen.sh` fail there.

**5. `evals/harness/took-effect.sh:133` — code accepts more than the header says (low)**
- `all_phases_present` accepts a prefix when the status is `running`. The header (lines 18-19) lists only `cap_failure|agent_error|interrupted`.
- A run whose `pipeline.json` still says `running` passes on a partial phase list.

**6. `evals/harness/run-arms.sh:121` — `--max-usd 0.0` is accepted (low)**
- The check only rejects the literal string `"0"`. `0.0` and `0.00` pass `usd_ok`, despite the message "must be a positive amount".
- Every trial is then cut immediately (0+est > 0).

**7. `evals/harness/validate-suite.sh:331` — the mount-owned check on a hidden dest can be bypassed (low)**
- `rel_ok` accepts `./.claude/x.py`, and `"./.claude/x.py".split("/")[0]` is `"."`, so the check doesn't fire (verified).
- Normalising first (`os.path.normpath`) would close it.

**8. `evals/harness/spend.sh:152` — ledger rows that only carry `cost_usd` count as $0 (low)**
- `spend.sh` reads only `cost_micro_usd`. Such rows are still counted in `ledger_rows` and are not reported as skipped.
- `pipeline-run.sh:771` handles the same ledger format with a fallback, `(.cost_micro_usd // ((.cost_usd // 0) * 1000000))`, so the two scripts disagree on the same data.

**Doc nit:** `evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml:36` says `cost_hint` is the "run-arms … est_next fallback". `run-arms.sh:174-178` only reads `cost_hint` from its own recall suite file (`evals/suites/$SUITE.yaml`, line 133), never from `ablation-2.0.yaml`. The map branch (reading the `review-catch` key) only matters if a recall suite declares a map.

## Checked and fine
- Spend-cap arithmetic in `budget_gate`: the RA-6 and RA-9 walk-throughs hold, `reap 0` can't spin forever, and cut vs. wait ordering is correct.
- `spend.sh` totals, dedup and `--since` filtering match the fixtures.
- In `ablation-row.sh`, `modelinv_lines` (1-based, inclusive) matches how `pipeline-run.sh` counts lines, and `cost_usd` = 3.2 matches `pipeline.json`'s `spent_usd`.
- `took-effect.sh` frontmatter awk, prefix matching, `index`-based `task_types` checks, and the screen-batch exclusion from the suite STATUS aggregate.

Scratch copies are in `/home/evaluser/scratch-a/` (`/tmp` is mounted noexec here, so the stubs can't run from it).

input.content:
head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:266 — integrity_clean never enforces the trusted digest: a mismatch between arm_evidence.manifest_sha256 (the harness's hash of checksums.json at mount time) and the current sandbox/.claude/checksums.json only changes the evidence text, and the rule still returns 0. An agent that edits a .claude/ file and rewrites that file's entry in the agent-writable manifest passes the rule (reproduced: CLAUDE.loa.md was edited, its hash updated in checksums.json, and the rule reported "integrity_clean OK"). Files added under .claude/ that are not in the manifest are never examined either. The rule should fail when filesha != msha.
head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:144 — mount_prompt_surface's copies (lines 144, 146, 150, 152, 154) have no `|| return 2`. execute-agent.sh:207 calls the function as `... || exit 2`, and bash suspends `set -e` inside a function called that way, so a failed cp is ignored, the function returns 0 and the agent runs on an incomplete prompt surface. In base these copies ran at top level under `set -euo pipefail` and aborted the run (reproduced with an unreadable rules file: base exits 1, head runs the CLI). This contradicts the "WITHOUT behaviour change" claim and the lib's own contract ("2 when a step cannot take effect"). The whole-tree cp at line 131 is checked; these are not.
head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:235 — toggles write through symlinks: cp -a (lines 131/144/150) keeps symlinks from the prompt tree, then the effort toggle (`cat "$tmp" > "$f"`, here) and the .checksum refresh (line 342, `printf > "$mc.checksum"`) write to wherever the link points. A PR-controlled .claude/ whose SKILL.md is a symlink to a host file gets that host file edited (reproduced). find -type f at line 391 skips symlinks, so the regenerated manifest does not cover them either. This contradicts "files, never a symlink" (line 18) and "toggles hit the SANDBOX COPY only".
head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:513 — init_sandbox_beads runs `bash <ws>/.claude/scripts/beads/update-beads-state.sh` (code copied from --source-tree) on the host driver with the driver's whole environment, AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK included, outside the container and the env-allowlist shim. This contradicts the trust-boundary rule stated at pipeline-run.sh:125 and sandbox-mount.sh:97-100 ("no harness script sources .claude/ code"). The pipeline-run.bats trust-boundary test only greps for `source`, so it does not catch this.
head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:178 — the new `gen-checksums.sh --check` gate compares against the committed .claude/checksums.json, which MP-6 (tests/unit/check-manifest-paths.bats:88) treats as committed. This PR changes about 16 tracked .claude/ files (model-config.yaml and its .checksum, CLAUDE.loa.md, check-loa.sh, preflight.sh, generated-model-maps.sh, the bridgebuilder generated files, the pricing test) but does not regenerate .claude/checksums.json, so the gate it adds should report `changed:` drift and fail CI on this PR.
head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:212 — the new "Run eval harness tests" step and the manifest gate (line 175) are not wired into the workflow's push/pull_request `paths:` filters (lines 23-72 list neither evals/**, tools/gen-checksums.sh, tools/check-manifest-paths.sh, .claude/checksums.json, .claude/loa/** nor .claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/**). A PR that touches only those paths never runs either step, so harness regressions and manifest drift can merge unchecked.
head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:506 — the new --max-usd accounting adds only `.executor.total_cost_usd` of the final row. On a transport retry, run_trial resets `executor='null'` (line 454), so attempt 1's spend is dropped, and a row whose second attempt fails before executing records cost 0. Spend is under-counted and the cap can be overshot, contradicting the header ("spent = executor-reported total_cost_usd of … completed and failed rows").
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:708 — the phase records bind `--arg label` and use `$label` (here and in the phases.jsonl writer at lines 816-826). `label` is a jq keyword, and jq 1.6, still the default on Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04, rejects the program ("syntax error, unexpected label"), so every phase dies as infrastructure_error. Reproduced: on jq 1.6, 40 of 52 pipeline-run.bats tests fail. Use a different variable name such as `$lbl`.
head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:285 — the object shorthand `{name, label, session_id, …}` does not compile on jq 1.6 (`label` is a keyword), so every row build exits 3, which is not among the documented exit codes (0/1/2). Write `label: .label` instead.
head/evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats:313 — the new negated assertions (`! grep …`, here and at lines 294, 295, 361, 481) can never fail a bats test unless they are the test's last command, because a `!` pipeline is exempt from errexit. The no-effort, no-inherited-ENFORCE and no-arm-id/hidden-leak checks therefore assert nothing. The `[ ] && [ ]` chains at lines 292, 293, 327, 485 and 486 likewise only check the last term. Use `run !` or `|| false`.
head/evals/tests/freeze.bats:38 — `! grep -qv …` (and `! grep -q '  smoke/'` at line 79) is not the last command of its test, so it cannot fail. The manifest line-format check and the "smoke is outside the manifest" check are not actually tested.
head/tools/check-manifest-paths.sh:80 — `git ls-files -- .claude` without -z C-quotes paths that contain non-ASCII bytes or `"`, while gen-checksums.sh (ls-files -z) writes the raw path as the manifest key. Such paths are reported as untracked and the gate exits 1 on a manifest that gen-checksums.sh --check accepts (reproduced with .claude/café.md). Use `-z` or `-c core.quotePath=false`.
head/.claude/scripts/preflight.sh:190 — the new count is every `git ls-files -- .claude` entry, but gen-checksums.sh only hashes tracked paths that are regular files in the work tree (symlinks to directories, gitlinks and deleted paths are skipped). The counts disagree, preflight reports "file count mismatch", and that is exit 1 under strict integrity_enforcement (reproduced with a tracked directory symlink).
head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:6 — the "WITHOUT behaviour change for the cycle-129 single-skill path" claim is wrong. Arm mode now rewrites .claude/checksums.json for every run (baseline included), adds manifest_files and manifest_sha256 to arm_evidence (previously {} for baseline), and unsets an inherited LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE (execute-agent.sh:211-222).
head/evals/tests/fixtures/mount-lib-stub.sh:24 — the stub mount library has drifted from the real lib: it emits `mount=whole_tree` where the real lib emits `mount=tree` (and pipeline-run.bats:245 asserts the stub's value), writes sprint.md for sprint_plan: false review-catch arms, ignores unknown toggles and names its evidence `effort_stripped`. Because pipeline-run.bats runs only against this stub, contract drift between pipeline-run.sh and lib/sandbox-mount.sh goes undetected.
head/evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation:69 — the Python dependencies are installed with ranges (`rfc8785>=0.1.4`, `jsonschema>=4.21`, `pyyaml>=6.0`, `httpx[http2]>=0.24.0`) although the header says the image's tool versions are the batch's pinned versions; a rebuild silently changes them. The `FROM rust:1-bookworm AS brbuild` stage (line 19) uses a floating tag and is never copied from, so it is dead code and breaks legacy (non-BuildKit) builds.
head/evals/harness/spend.sh:152 — ledger rows that carry only `cost_usd` are counted as rows but priced at $0. pipeline-run.sh:771 prices the same ledger with a `(.cost_micro_usd // (.cost_usd * 1e6))` fallback, so the spend report and the run cap disagree on the same data.
head/tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh:133 — `ls-files --cached --others` does not list paths removed with git rm or renamed away with git mv, so the overlay keeps files the change deletes, and the proof runs against a tree that is not the work tree.
head/tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh:105 — run_step calls overlay and init_downstream inside `if ! "$@"`, which suspends `set -e` in them. A failed cp, mkdir or git add inside overlay is ignored (only the last command's status counts), so the proof can report success on an incomplete mount.
head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:133 — all_phases_present accepts a prefix of the phase list when the status is `running`, which the header (lines 18-19, cap_failure|agent_error|interrupted only) does not allow. A record left by a SIGKILLed driver therefore passes the rule on a partial phase list.
head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:121 — only the literal string "0" is rejected, so `--max-usd 0.0` or `0.00` passes the "positive amount" check, and every trial is then cut immediately.
head/evals/harness/validate-suite.sh:331 — the mount-owned check on a hidden dest compares `d_.split("/")[0]`, so `./.claude/x.py` (accepted by rel_ok) yields "." and bypasses it. Normalise the path first.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

head/evals/tests/fixtures/mount-lib-stub.sh:24 — the stub mount library has drifted from the real lib: it emits `mount=whole_tree` where the real lib emits `mount=tree` (and pipeline-run.bats:245 asserts the stub's value), writes sprint.md for sprint_plan: false review-catch arms, ignores unknown toggles and names its evidence `effort_stripped`. Because pipeline-run.bats runs only against this stub, contract drift between pipeline-run.sh and lib/sandbox-mount.sh goes undetected.
head/evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation:69 — the Python dependencies are installed with ranges (`rfc8785>=0.1.4`, `jsonschema>=4.21`, `pyyaml>=6.0`, `httpx[http2]>=0.24.0`) although the header says the image's tool versions are the batch's pinned versions; a rebuild silently changes them. The `FROM rust:1-bookworm AS brbuild` stage (line 19) uses a floating tag and is never copied from, so it is dead code and breaks legacy (non-BuildKit) builds.
head/evals/harness/spend.sh:152 — ledger rows that carry only `cost_usd` are counted as rows but priced at $0. pipeline-run.sh:771 prices the same ledger with a `(.cost_micro_usd // (.cost_usd * 1e6))` fallback, so the spend report and the run cap disagree on the same data.
head/tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh:133 — `ls-files --cached --others` does not list paths removed with git rm or renamed away with git mv, so the overlay keeps files the change deletes, and the proof runs against a tree that is not the work tree.
head/tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh:105 — run_step calls overlay and init_downstream inside `if ! "$@"`, which suspends `set -e` in them. A failed cp, mkdir or git add inside overlay is ignored (only the last command's status counts), so the proof can report success on an incomplete mount.
head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:133 — all_phases_present accepts a prefix of the phase list when the status is `running`, which the header (lines 18-19, cap_failure|agent_error|interrupted only) does not allow. A record left by a SIGKILLed driver therefore passes the rule on a partial phase list.
head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:121 — only the literal string "0" is rejected, so `--max-usd 0.0` or `0.00` passes the "positive amount" check, and every trial is then cut immediately.
head/evals/harness/validate-suite.sh:331 — the mount-owned check on a hidden dest compares `d_.split("/")[0]`, so `./.claude/x.py` (accepted by rel_ok) yields "." and bypasses it. Normalise the path first.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

The verdict is **CHANGES_REQUIRED**: I wrote 22 findings to `/workspace/review.md`. Several of them undermine what this PR is meant to provide: mount integrity, sandbox isolation and spend caps.

**Most serious:**
- **The integrity check can be fooled** (`took-effect.sh:266`). `integrity_clean` compares the recorded manifest hash to the current one but passes either way. An agent that edits a `.claude/` file and also updates its entry in the manifest is reported clean. I confirmed this by reading the code; it was also reproduced in a scratch copy.
- **Copy failures no longer stop a run** (`sandbox-mount.sh:144`). After the code was moved into the library, a failed copy into the sandbox no longer stops `execute-agent.sh`. The agent then runs on an incomplete prompt surface. Before the change these copies aborted the run, so the "without behaviour change" claim is wrong.
- **Toggles follow symlinks out of the sandbox** (`sandbox-mount.sh:235`, `:342`). A PR-controlled `.claude/` containing a symlink gets the file it points to on the host edited.
- **Untrusted code runs on the host with secrets** (`sandbox-mount.sh:513`). `init_sandbox_beads` runs `.claude/scripts/beads/update-beads-state.sh`, copied from `--source-tree`, on the host with the full environment, including the Bedrock token. That contradicts the PR's own rule that harness scripts never run `.claude/` code.
- **The new CI gate will likely fail on this PR** (`bats-tests.yml:178`). About 16 tracked `.claude/` files change but `.claude/checksums.json` isn't regenerated. This assumes the manifest is committed, as one of the new tests (MP-6) states; the frozen PR only contains touched files, so I couldn't confirm it.
- **The new CI steps don't trigger on the files they cover** (`bats-tests.yml:212`). The workflow's path filters don't include `evals/**` or the gate scripts.
- **The spend cap undercounts** (`run-arms.sh:506`). When a trial is retried, the first attempt's cost is dropped. The retry code predates this PR, but the new `--max-usd` cap depends on it.

**Also in the review:**
- `pipeline-run.sh:708` and `ablation-row.sh:285` fail to compile on jq 1.6, which is still the default on Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04. Here, 40 of 52 `pipeline-run.bats` tests fail under jq 1.6. CI's newer jq accepts the code.
- Several new negated assertions in `arm-toggles.bats` and `freeze.bats` can never fail.
- The stub that `pipeline-run.bats` runs against has drifted from the real mount library, so the tests can't catch contract changes.
- Smaller issues:
  - path quoting in `check-manifest-paths.sh`;
  - a file-count mismatch in `preflight.sh`;
  - unpinned Python packages and a dead build stage in `Dockerfile.ablation`;
  - gaps in `fresh-mount-proof.sh`;
  - input checks that can be bypassed in `run-arms.sh` and `validate-suite.sh`.

**What I couldn't run:** the frozen PR holds only the 72 changed files, so some suites had to be checked by reading: `validate-suite.bats`, `freeze.bats`, `run-arms.bats`, and the full-repo cases of `arm-toggles.bats`. `took-effect.bats`, `ablation-row.bats` and `spend.bats` pass on jq 1.7.1. The model-config checksum, generated registries and version strings all check out.
